reason: At the base revision REGEX_FORMAT matches Y{1,4} but format() only implements YY/YYYY, so lone 'Y' and 'YYY' fall through to the timezone-offset fallback and produce offsets like '+0000' instead of the literal letter, contradicting the expected result.

After the change the format regex only matches YYYY|YY, so a single 'Y' is left untouched as a literal and 'YYY' is rendered as the two-digit year plus a literal 'Y' ('24Y'), exactly as the test expects.

The base revision already decodes percent-encoded path parameters in #getDecodedParam/#getAllDecodedParams when the value contains '%', so '%20' is returned as a space; the PR is only a refactor of existing behavior.
The refactor moves the identical 'contains %' check into the shared tryDecodeURIComponent utility, preserving the decoding of route parameters, so the handler still reads the decoded character.
Before the fix, reschedule writes the new score to Redis but never updates @score, so the same in-memory entry keeps reporting the stale pre-reschedule time, failing the test.
The fix sets @score = at.to_f after the zincrby call, so the held entry reference immediately reports the newly requested reschedule time, matching the expected result.
Parsing 'text/plain; charset=UTF-8' with a readable charset parameter is long-standing ContentType behavior in ktor-http; the pull request only touches Range header parsing and cannot affect it.
The change is confined to parseRangesSpecifier whitespace trimming; content-type parsing with charset parameters is unaffected and continues to work at the head revision.

The zip archiver at this revision has no mechanism to preserve source file modification times (entries end up with a default such as the DOS epoch 1980-01-01), and the unrelated logging-only pull request does not change archiving, so the test fails on both sides of it.

Re-archiving still produces entries without source-matching modification times at this revision; the ComposerRepository logging change is unrelated to the archiver, so both extractions show the 1980 default the test forbids.

The pull request only alters CredentialCache prefix comparison in System.Net and cannot affect System.Text.Json; async list deserialization of this shape is established behavior at this revision, so the case succeeds.
The System.Net credential cache change is unrelated to JSON serialization, so synchronous and asynchronous deserialization remain equivalent and neither throws at this revision.

The inet containment-or-equal operators <<= and >>= have long been supported in CockroachDB and work with ANY, and the cursor FETCH fix in the pull request is unrelated, so the statement parses and returns true at the base revision.
The head revision only changes WITH HOLD cursor FETCH FIRST handling; the inet >>= ANY comparison is unaffected and executes successfully returning true.
On the base revision the '::1' NO_PROXY entry becomes the mount pattern 'all://*::1', which the later URL parsing step cannot interpret, so client construction raises an error instead of succeeding.
After the fix IPv6 entries are bracketed as 'all://[::1]', a valid pattern, so the client is created successfully and normal requests still work.

The base revision's strict flag equality check in Series.str.match rejects every regex flag other than re.IGNORECASE, so passing the dot-matches-newline option (via flags or a compiled pattern) raises instead of honoring the option.
The fix restores support for flags like re.DOTALL both via flags= and on compiled patterns across dtypes, so 'a\nc' matches and 'ac' does not for both call styles.

The base revision mishandles freezing a chain containing a group followed by more than two tasks (issue #8890), so the serialized/reconstructed result tree loses child results for the group tasks and does not contain all four expected children.
The fix restores the previous task/result linkage after a mid-chain group, so freezing, serializing and reconstructing the chain preserves a child result for every task in both parallel groups.

At the base revision the '--' escape unconditionally switches the parser to trailing-values mode without honoring the current positional's value_terminator, so the first positional keeps capturing ('--check' included) and the second never receives it.

The fix gives the current positional's value_terminator precedence over entering trailing-values mode, so the first positional ends at '--' with value1/value2 and the remaining '--check' is handed to the second positional without a parse error.

At the base revision a post-startup OSC 11 response sets 'background' via nvim_set_option_value, which fires OptionSet and the background-driven colorscheme reapplication, so both autocommands trigger as the test expects.

The pull request deliberately wraps the OSC 11-driven background update in :noautocmd so it no longer triggers OptionSet (per the PR, OSC11 is not intended to fire it), so the test's expectation that both OptionSet and ColorScheme fire is not met at the head revision.

Required-field validation flagging an omitted mandatory field as invalid with a 'can't be blank' error is core, long-standing Ecto.Changeset behavior; the pull request only reorders @derive inspection at schema compile time and cannot affect it.

The compile-time dependency change in Ecto.Schema is unrelated to changeset validation, so required-field validation still marks the changeset invalid with the expected blank-field error at the head revision.
